title: Supply & Delivery of Site Investigations at Civic Square, Chorley
description:
Chorley Borough Council are seeking to appoint a supplier for the supply and delivery of Site Investigations at the Civic Square, Cleveland Street, Chorley. The objectives of these site investigations are to support future planning applications for redevelopment of the site and to support design stages, specifically:

•	To investigate the subsurface strata below the existing site with respect to future foundations / hard standing construction.

•	To determine the general chemical condition of site soils (suitability for re-use, remediation requirements & waste characterisation). 

•	To determine any contaminative impact on underlying groundwater and surface water.

•	To determine risk posed by ground/ hazard gases to future buildings and site users.

title: LPS CARE - Contract for the Provision of Extra Care Services at Tatton Gardens, Chorley - RFQ 15316904,1
description:
Extra care housing provides safe and secure self-contained accommodation for older adults who require varying levels of care and support to enable them to live independently in a home environment.
Tatton Gardens is a new scheme that is currently being developed by Chorley Council and is due to open in October 2022.  During office hours, Monday to Friday, the scheme will be staffed with council housing management staff and a concierge service is due to be provided during evening and weekends.
Lancashire County Council is looking to appoint a Service Provider to deliver Care and Support services at the new Scheme.
Tatton Gardens is located on Eaves Lane in Chorley. It will have 62 one-bedroom and two-bedroom apartments to rent for people aged 55 and over.
For further information, please see the attached tender documents.

title: Financial System
description:
Chorley Council is inviting tenders for a new financial system to encompass itself, South Ribble Council and relevant legal entities. The system will encompass an integrated debtor, purchase card, general ledger and procurement service to deliver financial information and reporting fit for purpose.

A detailed list of functionality requirements is included within the tender documents, but the emphasis is on improved processes and end user experience as well as an ability to work in system as well as exporting into spreadsheet software. Within the scope of the project is:

• General Ledger
• Accounts Payable (Creditors)
• Intelligent Invoice Scanning (OCR)
• Accounts Receivable (Debtors)
• Debt Recovery
• Procurement (Procure to Pay)
• Reporting
• Making Tax Digital
• Purchase Cards Monitoring System
• GDPR / Archiving
• Integration with all feeder systems (e.g. customer payments and payroll)
• Finance Server Transfer to Cloud (Procedure for retaining and archiving existing data)
• Access to Cloud based system via Citrix

Enhanced functionality required;
• Enhanced end-user experience (dashboard / simpler system interface)
• Simplified approval/workflow processes and access/authorisation segregation configuration
• Enhanced reporting capability for Finance and non-Finance users
• Balance sheet reconciliation module

title: Provision of Bikeability Training in Lancashire Lot 2: Burnley, Lot 12: Lancaster
description:
"Bikeability is the Department for Transport's (DfT) flagship national cycling training programme for school children in England. It is a practical cycle training programme which provides school children with a life skill and enables them to cycle confidently and competently. Bikeability funding is distributed annually to local highway authorities, which the Authority is classified as. 

An open procurement procedure was conducted by the Authority in early 2024 to establish a multi-lotted, multi-provider framework to deliver Bikeability training on behalf of the Authority for the periods 2024/2025, 2025/2026, 2026/2027 and 2027/2028. The Framework was divided into 12 Lots based on the districts of Lancashire: Lot 1: West Lancashire, Lot 2: Burnley, Lot 3: Chorley, Lot 4: Fylde, Lot 5: Hyndburn, Lot 6: Pendle, Lot 7: Preston, Lot 8: Ribble Valley, Lot 9: Rossendale, Lot 10: South Ribble, Lot 11: Wyre, Lot 12: Lancaster. During the procurement process, no tender responses were received for Lot 2: Burnley and Lot 12: Lancaster. 

The aim of this procurement is to establish service provision for Lot 2: Burnley and Lot 12: Lancaster. The framework will have an initial term of 12 months running from 1st April 2025 to 31st March 2026. There will be the option to extend beyond the initial term to a maximum of a further 24 months in tranches of 12 months. "
cpvDescriptionExpanded: Education and training services
awardedSupplier: Go Velo Ltd,Sporting NRG Ltd,Gorilla Brakes Ltd

title: NHSE875a Invitation to Tender - Alternative Provider Medical Service (APMS) - Withnell Health Centre
description:
North of England Commissioning Support is working for and on behalf of NHS Lancashire and South Cumbria Integrated Care Board (ICB) (the Contracting Authority), to commission Withnell Health Centre Alternative Provider Medical Service (APMS).
Premises are mandatory and are located at Withnell Health Centre, Railway Road, Withnell, Chorley, PR6 7PS.
The contract is for 10 years with the option to extend for 5 years subject to satisfactory financial and contractual performance and at the discretion of the Contracting Authorities. 
The expected start date of the contract is 01 April 2023.
The procurement will be available to view on the e-tendering portal on 7th September 2022, and the closing time and date for tender returns is by 12:00 noon on 19th October 2022.
The basic principles that mirror that of the open procedure will be followed for this procurement to test the capacity, capability, and technical competence of tenderers in accordance with the Light Touch Regime within The Public Contracts Regulations 2015
(as amended), ensuring a fair, open, and transparent process in accordance with NHS (Procurement, Patient Choice and Competition) (No. 2) Regulations 2013.
Accordingly, the subject matter of the contract has been scoped to consider the priorities of the Contracting Authority relating to "economic, social, and environmental well-being" by utilising the UK Government's Social Value Model.

title: TC076 - DPS for The Provision of Passenger Transport Services
description:
The Borough Council of Bolton ("the Authority") received tenders to be included on the Dynamic Purchasing System for the Provision of Passenger Transport Services which was subject to the information, specification and tender package.\r
\r
A Dynamic Purchasing System is, in effect, an open framework agreement to which new providers can apply to be appointed to during its life. During this period new providers will be able to gain entry onto the Dynamic Purchasing System. During this period, the Dynamic Purchasing System will re-open intermittently, during which periods new providers will be able to gain entry onto the Dynamic Purchasing System. It is envisaged that the Dynamic Purchasing System will be re-opened as and when there is a requirement by the Authority for further provision.\r
\r
The term of the Dynamic Purchasing System will be for 5 years. The Dynamic Purchasing System will commence on 5th September 2020.
